messages:
emma: Quick heads-up — we just marked the hosted streaming + tool-calling stack as 'stable' for general usage. This includes the new observability hooks and updated default backoff policy. Rolling this out to prod now. :tada:
mike: Nice — what's changed for latency-sensitive customers?
emma: Primary changes: 1) built-in request-level tracing (prefix sampling), 2) default batching_window lowered to 10ms for realtime routes, 3) a new soft-rate-limit layer that surfaces 429s earlier to avoid tail latency spikes. Full notes below.
sarah: Ops note — tracing will emit new span tags: service=hosted-streaming, route_id, model_variant. We'll start collecting on staging in 30m. If you need traces disabled, ping @eng-sre.
emma: Copy of ops snippet for toggling sampling:```bash
# turn off prefix sampling for a route
curl -X POST "$REDWOOD_API/admin/routes/ROUTE_ID/config" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"prefix_sampling": false}'
```
mike: Will the new soft-rate-limit change customer-visible error rates?
emma: Ideally fewer hard spikes — you'll see earlier 429s when queues build, but fewer OOMs and timeouts. We also added a metrics dimension: queue_length_breakdown per model_variant.
david: Legal check — any customer contract implications from changing default backoff? We shouldn't change SLAs without notice.
emma: Good call. This is an ops-side default; SLAs remain the same. We'll add a customer-facing note and 30-day opt-out window for Dedicated customers. Natalie, can CS draft the notice?
natalie: On it. I'll post a short email and a console banner template in the next 24h.
oliver: Any deprecations? I thought we were sunsetting the legacy websocket multiplexer.
emma: Yes — legacy ws-mux will be deprecated in 90 days. It will continue to work for existing apps but won't receive instrumentation. We'll publish a migration guide (ws -> unified-stream) this afternoon.
mike: Deployment plan? Canary then region-wide?
emma: Canary in us-west-2 (10% traffic) in 20m, then expand to all regions over 6 hours if metrics look good. Rollback hooks are in place.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: hosted-streaming v1.4 promoted to canary in us-west-2 — build 2026.03.21.1542 — status: in-progress
sarah: Watching latency p95 and queue_length_breakdown. Alert thresholds: p95 > 220ms OR queue > 500 -> auto-rollback.
mike: I'll watch cold-start errors for quantized variants.
emma: Thanks — big ask: if you see any client regressions, drop a short note here with the route_id and a minimal repro. We'll triage immediately. :pray: 
oliver: For partners on Dedicated, should we proactively schedule migration calls?
natalie: Yes — I have a list of 12 customers on legacy ws. I'll start reaching out tomorrow.
david: I'll review the customer notice before send.
emma: Summary: stable marking for streaming & tool-calling, new tracing, lower default batching_window for realtime, soft-rate-limits, legacy ws deprecation in 90 days, canary rolling now. Customer notice + migration guide coming. Thanks all. :rocket:
